newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen end slightly easier.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen end slightly easier.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract ended slightly easier on Monday, as its upperside proved heavy, traders said.
Wariness about recent high price levels is preventing euroyen futures from rising, a city bank trader said.
Traders said euroyen futures mostly shrugged off moves in the Japanese government bond (JGB) market and reacted little even when JGBs reached record highs.
The key June JGB futures contract set a record high for any benchmark JGB futures contract of 126.88 in afternoon trade on Monday.

It is hard to tell whether the recent surge in JGBs will persist, and this uncertainty may be making euroyen futures traders cautious about chasing the upperside in line with JGBs, the city bank trader said.
JGBs may fall, for example, if the results of the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey due on April 2 come out stronger than expected, the trader said.
The BOJ injected 200 billion yen into the money market on Monday, conducting a neutral money market operation on the first day of a new bank reserves reporting period.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.48 percent on Monday, up from Friday's 0.44 percent.
Traders said the key overnight call rate sank on Friday because banks had managed to pile up much of their necessary reserves before then.
They said the key rate rose back up on Monday, as demand for short-term funds remained strong.
Lending and borrowing of funds for periods of more than one month were still rare, a trader for another city bank said.
The firmness of the key overnight call rate remains unchanged, and demand for relatively cheap short-term funds remains strong, the trader said.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.54 percent. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent and one-month CDs were offered at 0.55 percent.
All CD rates were unchanged from the previous day.
